items.title: ProofPatch: Reviewing Lean Statements and Keeping the Reviews Valid as Formalizations Evolve
items.source_text: The kernel of the Lean proof assistant checks that a proof establishes its statement. Whether the statement says what was intended is left to human reviewers. This is the old problem of validating a specification, and it grows more pressing as language models write formal statements in bulk and agents edit formal developments continuously. We present ProofPatch, a tool that helps reviewers judge Lean statements and keeps their judgments valid while the development changes. A reviewer can ask the kernel targeted questions about a statement, such as whether a hypothesis is needed or whether a…
items.summary: ProofPatch helps reviewers judge Lean statements and keeps their judgments valid as formalizations change, using targeted kernel questions.

items.title: Autoformalization for Ambiguous Inputs: Precision, Coverage, and Cost across SQL and Logical Forms
items.source_text: Agentic systems translate natural-language requests into executable artifacts while managing ambiguity and inference cost. We evaluate seven autoformalization workflows on SQL and first-order logic benchmarks for ambiguous inputs. Across five SQL workflows, the raw model leads with F1 of 53.35% on AMBROSIA and 60.85% on AmbiQT. On AmP, DRIFT gains 15.98 F1 points over the raw model at 2.03 times its token cost, whereas LoC uses 18.65 times the raw model's tokens with lower F1. Within AutoCedar, structured interpretation lowers F1 by 6.44-6.95 points and raises AMBROSIA token use 2.2-fold…
items.summary: Evaluates autoformalization workflows translating ambiguous natural language into SQL and first-order logic, comparing F1 and token cost.

items.title: VerusWeave: A Benchmark for Proof Repair in Concurrent Verus Programs
items.source_text: Concurrent software underpins critical infrastructure, including operating systems and databases, yet thread interactions can have bugs that bypass conventional testing. Verus extends Rust with formal verification capabilities, enabling developers to specify, implement and prove the correctness of concurrent code in the same language. Although coding agents have been explored for automated proof construction, existing Verus benchmarks offer limited coverage of concurrency-specific examples that connect atomic operations to abstract protocols. To address this gap, we introduce VerusWeave, the…
items.summary: VerusWeave is a benchmark for proof repair in concurrent Verus programs, targeting coding agents on atomic operations and abstract protocols.

items.title: Automated Theorem Generation in First-Order Logic by Construction from Triangular Standard Contradictions
items.source_text: Automated theorem generation (ATG) seeks to construct new theorems rather than merely prove given conjectures. Existing approaches typically generate candidate statements that require subsequent proof or formal verification. We propose a constructive framework for ATG in first-order logic based on triangular standard contradictions. The method constructs minimally unsatisfiable clause sets from selected first-order literals, then forms theorems by retaining some clauses as premises and taking the negation of one clause, or a conjunction of clauses, as the conclusion. Minimal unsatisfiability…
items.summary: Constructive framework for automated theorem generation in first-order logic from minimally unsatisfiable clause sets.

items.title: Coinduction in Grounded Arithmetic
items.source_text: A grounded arithmetic counts a sentence true only when a terminating process establishes it; a sentence no such process settles has no value. Such a logic can state that an event happens, but not that it never happens under unbounded choice. This paper extends such a logic so that it can. The base is Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) with Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA)'s least-fixed-point reading and ground induction. It adds a separate greatest-fixed-point former $ν$ with Park's coinduction rule, proves that one former cannot carry both ground induction and coinduction, and adds a…
items.summary: Extends Reflective Grounded Arithmetic with a greatest-fixed-point coinduction former and proves a limitation on combining it with ground induction.

items.title: DAPS: Dependency-Aware Premise Selection for LLM Theorem Proving
items.source_text: LLM-based theorem proving in Lean 4 has advanced rapidly, but provers are difficult to leverage newly contributed lemmas, because retrieval skews toward popular foundational lemmas, leaving the right premises buried among hundreds of thousands of candidates. Existing neural selectors rank candidates by semantic similarity, with three intrinsic limitations: frequency-skewed retrieval, isolated pairwise ranking, and degradation on out-of-distribution queries such as competition problems and informal language. Given that mathematics is structured by dependencies rather than similarities, we…
items.summary: DAPS is a dependency-aware premise selection method for LLM theorem proving in Lean 4, addressing retrieval skew toward popular lemmas.

items.title: Iris on Indirection Theory: Lightweight Higher-order Ghost State
items.source_text: Today, semantic models of languages with concurrency and higher-order state are constructed using step-indexed predicates over resources and higher-order ghost state. There are two main lines of work for constructing such models. On the one hand, Iris provides these in full generality, at the cost of a large body of mechanised domain theory that is difficult to learn and port to new proof assistants. On the other hand, Indirection Theory is much simpler through the use of ordinary dependent types, but its foundation in separation algebra limits the expressiveness of its resource model…
items.summary: Proposes lightweight higher-order ghost state for semantic models using Indirection Theory with ordinary dependent types, as an alternative to Iris.

items.title: Algebraic World Model: From Exploration to Proofs
items.source_text: AI has made remarkable progress in mathematics, solving challenging problems with machine-checkable proofs in Lean, yet typically relying on predefined mathematical definitions and formal specifications. This raises a natural question: can it reason rigorously about an unknown world? We introduce the Algebraic World Model (AWM), a framework that turns interaction with unfamiliar environments into explicit mathematical models supporting formal reasoning. AWM explores the environment and develops executable Python hypotheses, continually testing and revising them against observations. It then…
items.summary: Algebraic World Model turns interaction with unknown environments into executable Python hypotheses for formal reasoning, mentioning Lean only as background.

items.title: Hammering with Vampire in Lean
items.source_text: We present Vampire-Hammer, a hammer for the Lean interactive theorem prover that discharges goals using the Vampire automated theorem prover and reconstructs proofs checked by the Lean kernel. Vampire-Hammer uses the Lean-auto framework to process goals and premises before dispatching them to Vampire for proof search. Doing so, we rely on standard TPTP problem formats and annotated TSTP proofs that support proof reconstruction. With a 10-second budget on 196,083 eligible Mathlib theorems, Vampire-Hammer solves 21,158 problems not solved by other evaluated tools within the same budget.
items.summary: Vampire-Hammer is a hammer for Lean that sends goals to the Vampire prover and reconstructs proofs checked by the Lean kernel, solving 21,158 extra Mathlib…

items.title: Semantic Path Orders are Generalized Weighted Path Orders
items.source_text: Monotonic semantic path orders (MSPOs) are powerful reduction orders, but their effective use in theorem proving and termination analysis raises three issues: efficient comparison of terms, ground totality, and a reduction-pair formulation. Inspired by weighted path orders (WPOs), we introduce generalized weighted path orders (GWPOs) which encompass both WPOs and MSPOs. GWPOs and MSPOs coincide as classes of reduction orders, thereby yielding efficient and ground-total subclasses of MSPOs. We further formulate the reduction-pair version of the GWPO for the dependency pair method, from which…
items.summary: Introduces generalized weighted path orders that coincide with monotonic semantic path orders, giving efficient ground-total reduction orders for theorem…

items.title: Construction and formal verification of a special topology on {\mathbb{Z}}^{n}: characterization of connected subsets
items.source_text: We examine whether the integers admit a topology whose connected subsets are precisely the sets of consecutive integers. The main result gives a construction for every integer lattice {\mathbb{Z}}^{n}, n>0; the answer for Z is then obtained as a corollary. We prove that the neighborhoods determined by the parity of the sum of the coordinates form a basis and that topological connectedness agrees exactly with accessibility by finite paths of unit lattice steps. We also present a deductive audit and the correspondence between this argument and a verification in Lean 4 and Mathlib, including…
items.summary: Constructs a topology on Z^n whose connected subsets are consecutive-integer sets, with the argument audited against a Lean 4 and Mathlib verification.

items.title: Deogen: Automatic Benchmark Generation for Reasoning over Policies
items.source_text: Language models are increasingly being deployed in regulated settings, where a model must apply given rules to the facts of a situation to determine a verdict. Benchmarking this capability, known as deontic reasoning, remains a costly and manual process, with existing datasets largely hand-crafted. In this paper, we present DeoGen, a scalable, automatic, and parametrizable benchmark generator for deontic reasoning. By autoformalizing policy rules to first-order logic, we can construct decision trees that capture possible outcome trajectories. Each path down a tree becomes a benchmark entry…

We prove that the program answers every query as a simple reference specification does, that each operation takes at most a fixed number of steps, independent of the number of…

items.source_text: Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in research-level problem solving, yet a comprehensive collection of such problems is still missing, and evaluating them on research-level problems remains challenging. We introduce OpenFrontiers, a cross-disciplinary resource that combines a structured corpus of open research problems with a retrospective benchmark of recently resolved problems in mathematics. The corpus records problem statements, context, progress, and other information for 12,151 problems. The benchmark contains 200 problems, 110 resolved in 2026 and 90 still…

items.title: GTFormer: A Syntax-Free Graph Network Alternative to Transformers for 8192$\times$ Length Extrapolation in Linear Time
items.source_text: Self-attention mechanisms have established the Transformer as the dominant backbone across natural language processing, source code intelligence, and automated theorem proving. However, all-to-all pairwise token comparison enforces a quadratic $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ compute and memory barrier alongside severe softmax attention dilution as sequence length $N$ scales beyond the training horizon. Inspired by recent advances in algebraic graph learning (\textbf{WPNet}), this work introduces \textbf{GTFormer}, a syntax-free hierarchical Graph Neural Network (GNN) that replaces flat self-attention for…

items.title: Global Choice without Excluded Middle in Dependent Type Theory
items.source_text: Diaconescu's theorem derives excluded middle from the axiom of choice, using propositional extensionality. We show that in dependent type theory without propositional extensionality, global choice alone does not imply excluded middle. We consider extensional Martin-Löf type theory with an impredicative universe of propositions included in the universe of types, extended with a global choice operator. We construct a consistent model of this type theory and show that the model refutes excluded middle and propositional extensionality. The model is built from staged sets, sets whose elements…
items.summary: Shows in dependent type theory that global choice without propositional extensionality does not imply excluded middle, via a consistent model.

items.title: Preserving Separation Logic Specifications through Compilation
items.source_text: Program specifications in separation logic describe ownership of resources and serve as logical interfaces for local reasoning. Compiler correctness, expressed as semantics preservation, does not by itself supply such an interface for compiled code, because it does not explicitly relate source and target resources and assertions. We investigate WP-preserving compilation: when a compiler translates a source program, the weakest preconditions that the program satisfies in a separation logic carry over to the compiled program. Our proof technique consists of a resource-aware simulation over…
items.summary: Studies compilation that preserves separation logic weakest preconditions from source to compiled programs, using a resource-aware simulation proof technique.

items.title: A Counterexample to KL1 Completeness and a Complete Disjunctive Calculus
items.source_text: The logic KL$_1$ of Evans, Sergot and Stephenson formalizes Kant's rules as conditional imperatives $B \square\to C$ and permissives $B \diamond\to C$ over acts. Its consequence relation is operational: a rule follows from a set of rules when adjoining it leaves the set of outcomes unchanged for every input. The authors proved their calculus sound and conjectured that it is complete. We show that the conjecture fails: for distinct atoms $b,c,d$ the rules $\top \diamond\to b \lor d$, $b \diamond\to c$, $d \diamond\to c$ and $c \square\to b \lor d$ entail $\top \diamond\to c$, which is not…

items.title: Polymorphic First-Class Environments
items.source_text: First-class environments expose runtime environments as ordinary values and support a substitution-free, environment-based operational semantics. They also support applications such as first-class modules, dynamic composition of environment fragments, and sandboxing via local environments. Existing environment-based calculi, however, are mostly studied in a simply typed setting and stop short of System F and polymorphism. We present $F_E$, a polymorphic calculus with first-class environments that conservatively extends System F with a small-step environment semantics. $F_E$ eliminates all…
items.summary: Presents F_E, a polymorphic System F extension with first-class environments and a small-step environment semantics.

items.title: Proof Repair and (Co)algebra Equivalences
items.source_text: Maintaining formal proofs in response to breaking changes in their dependencies is a major challenge of proof engineering. Proof repair is a kind of proof automation that lessens the burden of this challenge by automatically adapting proofs in response to those changes. While proof repair is well understood through an algorithmic lens, it has, until now, been poorly understood through a theoretical lens. We address this gap by giving the first foundational treatment of proof repair, focusing in particular on type-theoretic proof repair in response to changes in datatypes. Our key insight is…
items.summary: Gives a first foundational treatment of type-theoretic proof repair for changes in datatypes, using (co)algebra equivalences.

Our main tool is a structure theorem for the components; together with a finite computation, it shows that every component has weight (the sum of the probabilities that its conditions fail) at most $3/4$, uniformly in $n$. Combined with the classical character-sum method…

items.title: Counting by the Book: Verifying Alaska's Ranked-Choice Elections
items.source_text: We present Alaska's ranked-choice elections as a case study in Formally Verified Democracy, a program to establish election results through formally checked proofs. Across 115 ranked-choice contests in Alaska since 2022, we identify 75 ballot records across 10 contests that were counted differently from this interpretation by a program reproducing the published results, without changing any winners. We trace these differences to overvotes and duplicate rankings…
items.summary: Formalizes Alaska's ranked-choice tabulation rules in Lean and verifies the implementation, finding 75 ballot records across 10 contests counted differently.

items.title: Inductive Grounded Arithmetic: Goodstein, the Hydra, and $Γ_0$
items.source_text: What does a recursive definition mean in a grounded logic, where a sentence is true only if a terminating process makes it so? This paper takes Kripke's answer for truth, the least fixed point, as a rule. Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) writes any recursive definition as one self-referential term; Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA) adds the elimination rule for every positive one, making each an inductive definition. IGA is omega-sound and proof-grounded: sound and complete for a semantics whose certificates are its own proofs. IGA proves Goodstein's theorem, the Kirby-Paris hydra game…
items.summary: Extends Inductive Grounded Arithmetic with inductive definitions, proving Goodstein's theorem and the Kirby-Paris hydra game in a grounded logic.

items.title: Efficient Proof Generation for Lean Statements with Multiple Candidate Answers
items.source_text: In formal systems such as Lean 4, efficiently finding answers to mathematical problems and generating verifiable proofs is an important task in automated mathematical reasoning. In the traditional way where an upstream solver provides multiple candidate answers, the common workflow requires searching for proofs for each candidate separately, incurring redundant computational cost. To this end, we propose a joint proof framework that integrates candidate answer selection, answer supplementation, and formal proof generation into a unified reasoning process. At its core is a trained prover that…
items.summary: A joint proof framework that selects candidate answers, supplements answers and generates formal Lean 4 proofs in one reasoning process.

items.title: lean-qverify: Bridging Qiskit and Lean 4 for Formal Quantum
items.source_text: Hello, I recently put together a small project called *lean-qverify*, which grew out of my interest in applying formal methods to verify quantum circuits. items.summary: lean-qverify bridges Qiskit and Lean 4 by checking exported OpenQASM 3 quantum circuits such as Bell and GHZ with proofs.

items.title: Unit: a type checker for dependent type theory
items.source_text: We present Unit, a type checker for dependent type theory with a module system in the tradition of Automath and a uniform treatment of definitions. There is no unification, no instance search, no tactics and no unfolding heuristic, so the work of checking can be observed and compared with the informal proof. With Unit we have checked a model of univalent type theory, synthetic algebraic geometry, and synthetic Stone duality with its cohomology, and results in commutative algebra, like finite free resolutions and Zariski Main Theorem. items.title: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving
items.source_text: While progress in informal mathematics has come largely from scaling the chain-of-thought and agentic reasoning of frontier language models, formal theorem proving has increasingly relied on human-designed workflows around these models, such as planning, decomposition, and orchestrating specialized provers. This raises a bitter-lesson question: can a simple agentic loop that scales test-time compute match these workflows? The answer matters as formal verification must scale to keep up with frontier models producing research mathematics, yet new workflows rarely settle it, as their gains are…
items.summary: Tests whether a simple agentic loop scaling test-time compute can match human-designed workflows for automated theorem proving in formal verification.

items.title: Numina Fuse: Interactive Autoformalization in Lean 4
items.source_text: Numina Fuse is an agent-native application for formalizing mathematics in Lean 4. Since Lean can compile while not representing its intended informal meaning, and agents now write Lean faster than people can read it, we built Fuse around human supervision of agent work. A user works with an AI orchestrator on a Lean project and supervises it through views of the blueprint, the dependency graph, and the Lean code, while the backend keeps the project's derived state and runs agents for hours without the user present.
